title: Epoch-merge translational loss causes quota misattribution for legacy namespace anchors
text:
Epoch-merge translational loss causes quota misattribution for legacy namespace anchors

description:
Summary: Intermittent misattribution of quota consumption was observed when epoch merges occur for namespaces that were created prior to the v2 policy rollout ("legacy namespace anchors"). The symptom is that per-key and per-route counters appear to remain unchanged while org-level aggregates rise, resulting in downstream silent throttle events for keys that should have remaining allowance. This ticket tracks investigation, temporary mitigations, and a long-term fix.

symptoms:
Customers report sudden per-key throttles despite low per-key counters in the console
Org-level billing spikes without corresponding per-route token events
Incidents correlate with shard rebalances and epoch merge logs
Incidents more frequent for orgs with long-lived namespace anchors created before policy-v2 migration

steps_to_reproduce:
Provision a legacy namespace anchor (created pre-policy-v2) and attach multiple route aliases (including wildcard aliases)
Seed traffic from a single API key hitting multiple routes with short-lived bursts and different priorities (foreground + background)
Trigger a planned shard rebalance or simulate an epoch merge by replaying consolidated policy snapshots
Observe metrics: per-key per-route counters, org aggregated counters, and enforcement decisions around the merge window
Reproduce the mismatch when a KV cache TTL reset coincides with the policy epoch translation step

impact:
High — affects accounting correctness and can cause unexpected throttling or billing variance for affected customers. Surface customer support tickets and potential revenue reconciliation.

root_cause_hypothesis:
During epoch merge the policy translator performs a lossy translation for legacy namespace anchors: route-level deltas that were stored with anchor-relative keys are being folded into org-level buckets due to a namespace key normalization bug. The translator uses a fallback anchor id when the original anchor mapping is missing or stale, which leads to aggregate-only attribution. This is amplified when KV cache TTL resets and shard leader changes occur during the same window, causing racey writes to the aggregation path.

evidence_collected:
Trace samples showing accept/allow decisions with empty per-key delta writes but non-empty org aggregate writes
Edge logs from two failed reproductions where epoch merge timestamps align with TTL expiry
Customer request IDs and support tickets TLDR showing timeline correlation
Sampling of DB writes shows anchor id swapped to zero-value during translator fallback

short_term_mitigation:
Add a conservative rollback: during epoch merge, stall translation commit until anchor mapping presence is verified (deploy as hotfix for affected regions)
Deploy temporary telemetry that emits a 'translation-loss' metric when a translator sees an anchor resolution miss
Notify support and create a monitoring dashboard that flags org spikes without per-key counterparts

long_term_proposal:
Fix translator to preserve per-route/per-key delta routing by embedding explicit anchor lineage in epoch snapshots
Add an idempotent reconciliation job: scan recent org-level aggregates and attempt to reconcile missing per-key deltas using request-level traces for the merge window
Strengthen shard handoff semantics so that TTL resets cannot race with epoch commit (introduce two-phase commit for translator writes)
Add unit + fuzz tests for translator across anchor creation/rename/deprecation workflows

proposed_changes:
runtime: translator: store anchor lineage metadata in epoch snapshot (schema bump)
enforcer: validate delta writes have non-null route/key tags before committing to org aggregate
kvs: add conditional write guard to prevent zero-anchor fallback during merge
observability: emit translation-loss event with request_id and anchor_id for debugging

acceptance_criteria:
No incidents matching the reproduction steps for two full shard cycles in staging
Per-key counters and org aggregates remain consistent (<1% variance) across synthetic merge tests
Reconciliation job can reconstruct missing deltas for a sampled 24h window with >95% success for sampled events
Hotfix rollback path validated and runbook posted to runbook-docs link

notes:
2026-02-25: triaged by SRE and Billing; assigned to Liam for root cause analysis
2026-03-02: reproduced in staging with controlled TTL expiry sequence; attached traces to PR
2026-03-04: decision to ship temporary stall hotfix to us-west-2; hotfix rolled out 2026-03-05
2026-03-08: hotfix reduced customer incidents by ~70% for affected customers; further work on translator required
2026-03-10: proposed schema change reviewed by runtime arch; concerns about migration cost raised — agreed to perform a canary on non-production orgs first
Follow-ups: create runbook for customer refund/reconciliation and schedule cross-team postmortem after fix deploy
